walk: C1021 (collections 1016-1022, November 2026): the route and the count door walked blind from 1948 on first prints and release days (1948-60 on the documented BLS and DOL release days, collections 962 and 1020); the fed-shock door from 1954 and the job-losers door from 1967 (the series begin there). 13 of 13 recessions since 1948 called (2024 by the job-losers door on 5 January 2024), no false alarm; the plateau, noise, quiet-world and 78-world batteries 0 false alarms (RECORD-1021). Record cut 2024-07-01: every call after it is live.

notes.vintage: every monthly pillar - the unemployment rate, payrolls, the unemployed count, job losers, job openings, industrial production - is read within the vintage that stood on the day (ALFRED); weekly claims from the Department of Labor's first prints; the Baa yield, the funds rate and the Treasury yields are monthly averages known the day after month end (Baa read the 7th); the S&P 500 is never revised
notes.arithmetic: every pillar is a sign: on at or above its line; a reading equal to its line is at the line
notes.doors: the route needs all seven pillars on the same release day; each door is its own call; any one opens the episode
notes.closers: v3.76's labour closer and its confirmations, unchanged (collection 310)

objects_precise.survey_week: the insured rate in the week whose Saturday is nearest the 12th (a tie to the earlier), read against the lowest of the prior 52 monthly readings (four and a third years); from 2 August 1975 the Department's printed seasonally adjusted rate (the earliest release of each week), before it the lab's weekly construction (preweek.py: printed state counts, the lab's seasonal adjustment, the Fieldhouse denominator); a month is not read until its week is out
objects_precise.state_breadth_rates: each state's insured rate as printed on page 8 of the weekly release, 2002-11-16 to 2020-04-18 (46638 state-weeks); FRED's current file before and after
objects_precise.claims_before_2002: the weekly claims and the insured rate as printed, with their release days, from 2 August 1975 (E66); the walk reads the same table (v3.76)
objects_precise.search_terms: the search week reads Google searches for "unemployment" alone (v3.76, E79)
objects_precise.paper_spread: the 13-week mean against the lowest 13-week mean of the 39 weeks ending with the current week
objects_precise.market_gate: the S&P 500 against its highest close of the 20 trading days ending with the close read
objects_precise.closer_c_rate: the insured rate's four-week mean is rounded to a tenth before its fall from the 26-week maximum is taken
objects_precise.k_release: a close by K is dated by the release of the continued-claims week that fired (the week + 12 days)
objects_precise.vacancy_before_2010: the vacancy rate before July 2010 is the Petrosky-Nadeau and Zhang reconstruction (help-wanted index, then JOLTS as now published), not a print

core: C1021: one starter, four ways in, all read on the release day from first prints. The route: seven pillars on the same day - insured unemployment (NSA, 4-week sum) above a year earlier; job openings growing slower than initial claims (passes when no openings print stands); the S&P 500 below its close a year earlier on any of the last 25 days; industrial production below its 12-month high; the Baa yield above its 12-month low; the unemployment rate's two-month average 0.3 above the two months before (0.2 with payrolls falling); payrolls below their 12-month high and below last month. The count door: the unemployed count's first print at a 12-month high of first prints, claims (seasonally adjusted in real time) at a 365-day high of prints, the market below a year earlier. The fed-shock door: the funds rate up 1.5 points in a month. The job-losers door: job losers up 15 log points on the year, after the 10-year minus 1-year spread was negative in any of the prior 12 months. A call opens an episode when none stands and more than 183 days have passed since the last close. The closers and the damage grade are v3.76's, unchanged.
